_why: Won his eligibility back in court after the official roster page had already dropped him. wvusports.com still lists last season's team only, so the nightly scrape cannot find him and he would otherwise show with no photo, bio or stats.
bio:
West Virginia (2025-26)
• Named to the College Basketball Crown All-Tournament Team
• Started all 34 games he played in
• Averaged 11.9 points and 5.2 rebounds per game
• Shot 54.1% from the field
• Led the team with 45 blocked shots
• Finished with 15 points and eight rebounds against Oklahoma in the Crown
• Had 15 points and six rebounds against Creighton in the Crown
• Finished with 14 points and seven rebounds vs. Stanford in the Crown
• Had 11 points and seven rebounds against BYU in Big 12 Tournament
• Scored 14 points at Kansas State and against UCF
• Had 18 points and nine rebounds (seven offensive) in win over BYU
• Finished with 12 points at Oklahoma State
• Scored 10 points with six rebounds against Utah
• Finished with 11 points and eight rebounds in the win at UCF
• Recorded a team-high 21 points on 10-of-14 shooting vs. Texas Tech
• Scored 11 points at Cincinnati
• Had a game-high 19 points against Baylor
• Scored 12 points to go with nine rebounds vs. Kansas State
• Recorded 15 points at Arizona State
• Finished with 12 points and nine rebounds against Colorado
• Had 18 points (16 in first half) against Kansas
• Missed the Iowa State game due to injury
• Was 7-of-7 from the field and 3-of-3 from 3-point range to finish with 18 points, seven rebounds, four assists and four blocks vs. Ohio State
• Had 12 points vs. Coppin State
• Finished with nine points and five rebounds vs. Mercyhurst
• Scored 11 points with three blocks against Xavier
• Had nine points, five rebounds and four assists vs. Lafayette
• Recorded a career-high 26 points, including 11-of-15 from the field and 3-of-4 from 3-point range, and seven rebounds vs. Lehigh
• Finished with 12 points, nine rebounds and five blocks vs. CampbellHad a double-double in his first career start with 11 points and 13 rebounds vs. Mount St. Mary's
Prior to West Virginia
• Comes to West Virginia from North Texas, where he played last season
• Last year at North Texas, he was named American Athletic Conference First Team All-Conference and AAC Sixth Man of the Year
• Played in all 36 games and came off the bench in all 36 games, averaging 11.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 blocks per game
• Among all AAC players, he made the largest increase in points per game from the previous season
• His 421 total points off the bench were the second most in the nation among all reserves and only one point behind the leader
• His 178 total rebounds off the bench were the fourth most in the nation and 39 total blocks off the bench were the sixth most in the nation
• Scored in double figures 21 times and scored a career-high 20 points twice
• Had a double-double with 20 points and 13 rebounds and five blocks against Temple, the first time that stat line happened at UNT since 2013
• Scored more than 15 points 12 times, including 18 points at nationally-ranked Memphis
• His 39 blocks led the team and had the team’s second-highest scoring average at 11.7 points per game, while shooting 47.8% from 3-point range
• Played his first two collegiate seasons at Florida Atlantic
• In 2023-24, he scored a season-high 13 points against Eastern Michigan
• In 2022-23, he played in 21 games, helping FAU reach the 2023 Final Four
• Graduated from Calvary Christian Academy in Florida in 2022
• Helped lead CCA to the 2022 Florida High School Athletic Association 4A state championship, a No. 3 end of season national ranking and a 26-2 overall record
• Prior to attending CAA, he was at Forest High School in Ocala, Florida, where he was named the Marion County Boys Basketball Player of the Year
Personal
• Son of Gassete Lorient and Nobrens Lorient
• Pursuing a Regents Bachelor of Arts degree
• Birthday is April 29
